This study introduces a novel Poisson autoregressive model designed to accommodate time-varying parameters, specifically addressing the challenge of modeling count data where the autoregressive coefficient fluctuates over time. The proposed framework is established within a rigorous probabilistic setting, and the paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the model's asymptotic properties, including consistency and asymptotic normality for the maximum likelihood estimators. Furthermore, the authors demonstrate the practical utility of this approach through a simulation study and an empirical application to real-world data.

This study introduces a new method for measuring aerosol optical depth (AOD) using stellar photometry, which offers a more efficient and cost-effective alternative to traditional techniques. The approach leverages the fact that aerosols scatter light, causing a measurable dimming of starlight that correlates directly with AOD. By analyzing the light curves of stars observed by the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF), the method successfully recovers AOD values with an accuracy of 0.005, outperforming the 0.015 accuracy of the standard ZTF pipeline. Furthermore, the technique is capable of detecting rapid changes in AOD, such as those caused by dust storms, with a time resolution of 15 minutes. This capability is particularly valuable for monitoring dust events in the Atacama Desert, where the ZTF operates, and could be applied to other regions to enhance our understanding of atmospheric dust dynamics.

This study introduces a novel configurational sampling method for molecular systems, termed the Sturdy and Effective Configurational Molecular Sampling through Langevin Dynamics (SECSMLD) algorithm. The approach integrates a robust, efficient, and straightforward Langevin dynamics (LD) scheme with a newly developed, highly effective configurational bias Monte Carlo (CBMC) technique. The SECSMLD algorithm is designed to be both computationally efficient and capable of handling complex molecular structures. To demonstrate its efficacy, the method was applied to the self-assembly of block copolymers, specifically investigating the phase behavior of a diblock copolymer system. The results indicate that SECSMLD is a powerful tool for exploring the phase behavior of block copolymers and other complex molecular systems.

This study introduces a novel approach to evaluating automatic image descriptions (AIDs) by incorporating human reference information. The proposed method, termed Human Reference-based Automatic Description Evaluation (HRADE), functions as a hybrid system that combines the strengths of both reference-based and non-reference-based evaluation techniques. In this framework, human reference information is utilized to generate a set of non-reference features, which are then integrated with existing non-reference features to form a comprehensive feature set. This combined set is subsequently employed to train a non-reference-based description evaluation model. Experimental results demonstrate that HRADE outperforms current state-of-the-art methods, achieving a correlation coefficient of 0.800 on the Flickr30k dataset and 0.790 on the MS-COCO dataset.

This study explores the geometric field theory intricacy of the Euler-Arnold equations, which govern the dynamics of rigid body rotation. By examining the associated Euler-Poincaré equations, we demonstrate that the geometric field theory for rigid body rotation is equivalent to the geometric field theory for the Euler-Arnold equations. Furthermore, we establish that the geometric field theory for the Euler-Arnold equations is equivalent to the geometric field theory for the Euler-Poincaré equations. Finally, we show that the geometric field theory for the Euler-Poincaré equations is equivalent to the geometric field theory for the Euler-Arnold equations.

We present a comprehensive analysis of the baryon and meson production cross sections in proton-proton collisions at the LHC, utilizing data from the ALICE experiment. Our study focuses on the energy range spanning from 7 to 13 TeV, examining the behavior of these cross sections across the full spectrum of available charged hadron species. By fitting the data to a specific functional form, we successfully describe the observed trends and project the cross sections for the production of additional baryon and meson species. These predictions are derived from the established patterns of the known hadrons, offering insights into the yields of currently unobserved or less-studied particles within this collision regime.

This study introduces a novel broadband waveforming technique designed to simultaneously transmit data and power over a single carrier, leveraging a single-input single-output (SISO) orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) framework. The proposed method employs a single transmit antenna and a single receive antenna, utilizing a single carrier to deliver both data and power to a load. The core innovation involves a specific waveform design that ensures the load receives the required power while the receiver decodes the data. The paper demonstrates that this approach achieves a significant performance boost compared to traditional single-carrier methods, which rely on multiple antennas and multiple carriers to accomplish the same dual objectives.

This study introduces a theoretical framework for adjusting the Parton Distribution Functions (PDFs) of the proton, designed to incorporate new experimental data. The proposed method is applicable to any existing PDF set and relies on a specific fitting function to model the PDFs. This function is constructed from a linear combination of the original PDFs and a set of basis functions, which are derived from the original PDFs themselves. The fitting function is optimized to minimize the $\chi^2$ value, thereby ensuring the best possible fit to the new data. The framework is demonstrated using the CT14 PDF set, where it successfully incorporates new data from the LHCb experiment regarding the $W$ and $Z$ boson charge asymmetries. The results indicate that the new data significantly impact the $d$-quark PDF at low $x$ values, with the magnitude of this effect increasing as the $Q^2$ scale decreases.

This study introduces a linearized model designed to simulate the response of a turbulent jet fire to acoustic excitation, employing an active flame method. The model incorporates a linearized version of the G-equation, which describes the flame front's propagation, alongside a linearized form of the Favre-averaged Navier-Stokes equations to represent the surrounding flow field. The resulting linearized system is solved using a spectral method, with the flame front's evolution tracked via a Lagrangian approach. The model's validity is confirmed through comparisons with direct numerical simulation (DNS) data, demonstrating its capability to accurately predict the flame's reaction to acoustic disturbances. Furthermore, the model is utilized to investigate the flame's response to various acoustic frequencies and amplitudes, revealing that the flame's reaction is highly sensitive to both parameters. Specifically, the study identifies a critical frequency threshold; below this limit, the flame exhibits a linear response, whereas above it, the response becomes nonlinear. Additionally, the model shows that increasing the acoustic amplitude leads to a more pronounced nonlinear reaction.

This study introduces a nonlocal extension of the Einstein-Cartan-Sciama-Kibble (ECSK) theory, termed nonlocal ECSK (NECSK) theory. The framework is constructed using a nonlocal constitutive relation that links the torsion tensor to the spin density, thereby generalizing the local ECSK model. Within this nonlocal setting, the spin density is defined as a nonlocal function of the torsion itself. The paper derives the field equations for NECSK theory and demonstrates that the nonlocal constitutive relation can be inverted to express torsion as a nonlocal function of the spin density. Furthermore, the study examines the nonlocal constitutive relation under the assumption of a specific nonlocality kernel, showing that the resulting nonlocal torsion-spin relation aligns with the nonlocal constitutive relation derived from the nonlocality kernel. Finally, the paper investigates the nonlocal constitutive relation in the context of a nonlocal spin density, revealing that the nonlocality kernel can be reconstructed from the nonlocal constitutive relation.

The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is designed to probe the fundamental structure of matter by colliding protons at unprecedented energies. While the primary objective involves investigating the internal constituents of protons, the collisions also generate a variety of smaller systems. These include proton-proton interactions, proton-lead interactions, and lead-lead interactions. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the experimental capabilities and the current status of research regarding these small systems.

This study examines the repetition intervals of X-ray transients in neutron star binaries, analyzing data from 11 known systems. The findings reveal that these intervals follow a power-law distribution with a slope of approximately 1.5, indicating that shorter intervals are more frequent. Additionally, the research explores the nature of dormant X-ray binaries in the Galactic Centre, suggesting that their low luminosity is likely due to the absence of an accretion disk rather than a lack of mass transfer.

This study introduces a fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) algorithm designed to solve the bipartite vertex division problem. The objective is to partition the vertex set of a bipartite graph into two subsets, $A$ and $B$, such that the induced subgraph on $A$ contains no induced matching of size $k$, while the induced subgraph on $B$ contains no induced matching of size $l$. The algorithm achieves a running time of $O(2^{O(k+l)}n^{O(1)})$, where $n$ represents the number of vertices in the input graph.

This study introduces HyperDegrade, a novel technique designed to enhance the efficiency of software-based differential side-channel attacks. The method achieves this by accelerating the degradation of the target function, thereby enabling the extraction of secret keys from high-frequency processors (GHz) using only low-frequency sampling rates (MHz). Experimental results demonstrate that HyperDegrade successfully recovers AES keys from an Intel Core i7-10700K operating at 3.8 GHz, utilizing a sampling rate of merely 1.2 MHz.

This paper introduces a new unknotting procedure for both traditional and welded links, which are defined as equivalence classes of diagrams under specific moves. The method relies on a sequence of operations: first, the diagram is transformed into a welded link diagram; second, the diagram is converted into a planar diagram; and finally, the diagram is simplified into a trivial diagram. The authors demonstrate that this procedure is effective for traditional links and provide a concrete example of its application.

This study introduces a tactical multi-agent collaboration framework designed for robots operating within conventional networks, specifically addressing scenarios where both computational resources and communication bandwidth are limited. The proposed approach employs a hierarchical architecture: a high-level planner generates a global strategy, while a low-level controller executes the necessary actions. To ensure the global strategy remains feasible under strict resource constraints, the framework incorporates a novel algorithm for generating a globally optimal plan. Furthermore, the low-level controller utilizes a model predictive control (MPC) strategy to guarantee that the system adheres to these constraints during execution. The efficacy of this framework is demonstrated through a simulation of a tactical engagement involving two opposing teams of robots.

This paper introduces a novel embedding technique for the group of isometries of a hyperbolic surface into a product of hyperbolic spaces, known as a Garland product. The method relies on a specific decomposition of the surface into a collection of hyperbolic triangles, referred to as a Cartesian decomposition. This approach is designed to be applicable to any hyperbolic surface, regardless of its topological type.

The detection of gravitational waves (GWs) via laser interferometry is currently limited by quantum shot noise at high frequencies. To overcome this, we propose a novel approach: integrating a Sagnac interferometer into the GW detector's readout arm. This configuration, termed the sloshing-Sagnac interferometer, functions as a high-frequency quantum noise reduction system. We demonstrate that this design effectively mitigates quantum shot noise, achieving a 3 dB reduction in noise levels at 100 Hz and a 6 dB reduction at 1 kHz. Furthermore, we show that the sloshing-Sagnac interferometer can be combined with squeezed vacuum injection to further enhance high-frequency sensitivity.

This study examines the non-intersecting visibility regions within an XL-MIMO stochastic access protocol (SAP) operating under a non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) framework. The analysis focuses on a scenario where a single base station (BS) communicates with multiple user equipments (UEs) via NOMA, while the BS's transmit power is dynamically adjusted based on the visibility status of the UEs. The research derives the probability distribution function (PDF) for the non-intersecting visibility areas and evaluates the system's performance through the average achievable sum rate. Furthermore, the paper investigates the impact of the BS's transmit power on the non-intersecting visibility regions and the resulting system performance.

This study introduces a novel neural architecture for text generation that integrates $n$-gram linguistic models into a residual learning framework. The proposed method combines the predictive capabilities of $n$-gram models with the representational strengths of neural networks, offering a solution to the limitations of purely neural approaches, which often struggle with long-range dependencies and lack interpretability. By incorporating $n$-gram models as residual connections, the architecture effectively mitigates the vanishing gradient problem and enhances the model's ability to capture long-range contextual relationships. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that this hybrid approach outperforms existing neural baselines in both perplexity and BLEU scores, while also providing greater transparency regarding the underlying generation mechanisms.

In the 2020 United States election, the use of optical character recognition (OCR) to tally votes from paper ballots was a subject of intense scrutiny. This paper introduces iOCR, a novel method designed to enhance the accuracy of existing OCR systems by incorporating informed priors derived from the specific characteristics of the ballot being scanned. The authors demonstrate that iOCR significantly outperforms standard OCR approaches, achieving a 99.9% accuracy rate on a test set of 1,000 ballots from the 2020 election. Furthermore, the study reveals that iOCR is capable of identifying and correcting errors in the original OCR output, thereby improving the reliability of automated vote counting.

This study examines the atmospheric circulation patterns of terrestrial planets within a simplified global circulation model (GCM) that incorporates a single layer of idealized fluid. The model is designed to simulate the dynamics of a planet with a thick atmosphere, where the Coriolis force is the dominant factor in the momentum balance. By varying the rotation rate and the ratio of the planet's radius to its atmospheric depth, the research explores how these parameters influence the resulting circulation regimes. The findings reveal that the circulation structure is primarily determined by the Rossby number, which serves as a measure of the relative importance of inertial forces against the Coriolis effect. Specifically, the study identifies a transition from a cyclostrophic super-rotating regime—characterized by strong inertial forces and weak Coriolis effects—to a geostrophic turbulent regime, where the Coriolis force dominates and the flow becomes turbulent.

This study introduces a novel integral representation for the reciprocal Gamma function, derived from a recently established integral formula for the Gamma function itself. The proposed formulation is shown to be equivalent to the classical Euler integral and is demonstrated to be valid for all complex values of the argument. Furthermore, the paper provides a proof of the uniqueness of this representation.

We introduce a novel phase-space random quantum hydrodynamics (PSRQHD) framework designed to simulate the dynamics of interacting Bose fluids. This approach integrates the Wigner function with a stochastic hydrodynamic model, enabling the simulation of quantum effects such as interference and entanglement alongside classical hydrodynamic phenomena like shock waves and turbulence. The PSRQHD framework is constructed to be both exact and efficient, offering a significant improvement over existing methods by reducing computational costs by several orders of magnitude. We demonstrate the framework's capabilities through simulations of a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) in a harmonic trap, successfully reproducing the quantum interference pattern known as the Talbot effect. Furthermore, we apply the framework to investigate the dynamics of a BEC in a one-dimensional (1D) box, revealing the formation of a shock wave and the subsequent development of turbulence.

This paper presents a survey of the Instructor-Pupil (IP) framework, a method for knowledge acquisition in machine learning. The IP framework is designed to address the challenge of acquiring knowledge from a teacher, or instructor, who possesses the expertise to label data. The framework operates by having the instructor label a dataset, which is then used to train a model. This model is subsequently evaluated on a test set to assess its performance. The IP framework is applicable to various machine learning tasks, including classification, regression, and clustering. The paper also explores the framework's limitations and potential future directions.

This study introduces a concise function representation designed to facilitate the rapid computation of exact Maximum a Posteriori (MAP) inference and constrained optimization within graphical models. By leveraging this depiction, we establish a novel algorithm for exact MAP inference that achieves a time complexity of $O(n^2)$, where $n$ denotes the number of variables. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the proposed function depiction enables the efficient resolution of constrained optimization problems, specifically those involving cardinality constraints.

This study examines the stabilizer $Z_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ of the $n$-th symmetric power of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ under the action of the $n$-th symmetric group $S_n$. We establish that $Z_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ is isomorphic to the $n$-th Racah algebra $\mathcal{W}_n$, which is generated by the image of the universal enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ within the $n$-th symmetric power $S^n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Hilbert-Poincaré series of $Z_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ is a rational function, and we provide an explicit formula for this series.

This study introduces a novel, exact algorithm for computing the paired-permutation test statistic, specifically designed for structured test metrics. The proposed method offers a significant improvement over existing approaches by delivering precise results without the need for approximations. Furthermore, the algorithm is highly efficient, capable of processing datasets containing millions of observations within a matter of seconds.

We present a study of triangular flow, $v_3$, in Au+Au and Cu+Cu collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 200$ GeV, utilizing a multiphase transport (AMPT) model. Our analysis reveals that $v_3$ exhibits a linear correlation with the initial eccentricity, $\varepsilon_3$, across both centralities and collision systems. Furthermore, we observe that the ratio of $v_3$ to $v_2$ increases with the initial eccentricity, $\varepsilon_2$, and decreases as the system's multiplicity rises. These findings suggest that the initial geometry of the collision system plays a crucial role in determining the final flow patterns.

This study introduces a novel filter for the Poisson Multi-Bernoulli Mixture (PMBM) density, designed to address the challenge of tracking multiple targets where the number of targets changes over time. The proposed approach employs a partially lattice-based birth model, which is constructed by combining a lattice-based model with a constant velocity model. This hybrid strategy offers a balance between computational efficiency and accuracy, making it particularly suitable for scenarios involving high target velocities. The paper provides a detailed derivation of the filter and demonstrates its effectiveness through a simulation study focused on sensor management.

Soccer is a highly dynamic sport where the outcome of a match is often determined by the final minutes, making the development of effective decision-making strategies for coaches and players essential. This study introduces a novel deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework designed to optimize tactical choices during these critical end-game situations. The proposed approach employs a multi-agent architecture that learns optimal strategies through self-play, allowing the system to adapt to various opponent behaviors. Experimental results demonstrate that this method outperforms existing approaches, achieving a win rate of 58.3% against the best available strategy. Furthermore, the framework successfully identifies the most effective tactics for specific match contexts, offering valuable insights for real-world soccer management.

This study introduces a remote control system for a single-point Laser Doppler Vibrometer (LDV) designed to acquire two-dimensional (2D) measurements. The setup employs a single LDV sensor to capture velocity data at a specific point on a target surface, while a separate camera records the surface's displacement. By combining these datasets, the system reconstructs the full 2D velocity field. The proposed method was successfully tested on a vibrating membrane, demonstrating its capability to generate high-quality 2D velocity maps.

This study examines the spectral and orbital stability of solitary wave solutions for the Klein--Gordon equation coupled with an anharmonic oscillator. We establish that solitary waves are spectrally stable when the nonlinearity is subcritical, whereas they exhibit spectral instability in the supercritical regime. Additionally, we demonstrate that solitary waves are orbitally stable under subcritical nonlinearities and unstable under supercritical ones.

We examine the potential for detecting axion-like particles (ALPs) at Belle II through the decay of $B$ mesons, focusing on the specific channel $B^{\pm} \to K^{\pm} a$ followed by $a \to \gamma\gamma$. Our analysis indicates that the Belle II experiment could achieve a discovery sensitivity for ALPs with masses up to 1.5 GeV, provided the coupling constant $g_{a\gamma\gamma}$ exceeds $1.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ GeV}^{-1}$. Additionally, we explore the possibility of observing ALPs that evade detection in the displaced vertex search, which would occur if the coupling $g_{a\gamma\gamma}$ surpasses $1.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ GeV}^{-1}$.

This study introduces a novel contextualized language framework designed to identify semantic shifts in text, specifically focusing on the impact of the 2020 U.S. presidential election. The model was trained using a dataset of 1.5 million tweets collected from January 2016 through January 2021, with the objective of detecting changes in word meanings and usage patterns. The results demonstrate that the proposed contextualized language framework outperforms existing models in identifying semantic alterations, highlighting the necessity for such frameworks to capture evolving linguistic dynamics.

We examine the spin evolution of massive black holes (MBHs) in the context of ultralight boson (ULB) formation through the superradiance mechanism. Our analysis indicates that MBHs with masses exceeding $10^{8} M_{\odot}$ and spins surpassing 0.9 are likely to have already generated ULBs. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the spin evolution of MBHs with masses below $10^{8} M_{\odot}$ is significantly influenced by the presence of ULBs. Consequently, the spin evolution of MBHs with masses under $10^{8} M_{\odot}$ serves as a sensitive probe for detecting ULBs.

This study introduces a path integral approach for simulating the dynamics of a quantum harmonic oscillator under constant acceleration. The method employs a Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm to evaluate the path integral, enabling the calculation of the system's time evolution. We demonstrate that this technique effectively reproduces the analytical solution for the oscillator's dynamics. Furthermore, we apply the method to investigate the quantum Zeno effect, examining how frequent measurements influence the system's evolution.

This paper introduces a relational Hoare framework for quantum programs that incorporates anticipations, a feature enabling the prediction of future values. The framework is built upon a novel relational semantics for quantum programs with anticipations, which is defined using a relational abstract machine. This semantic model is proven to be sound with respect to a relational Hoare logic designed for quantum programs featuring anticipations. The logic itself is established through a relational variant of the standard quantum Hoare logic, augmented with specific rules to handle anticipations. Additionally, the paper demonstrates the logic's utility by applying it to verify a quantum algorithm for matrix multiplication.

The reconstruction of vector magnetic fields from spectropolarimetric observations is a critical task for solar physics, yet it is susceptible to biases introduced by the inversion algorithms themselves. This study investigates the origins of these biases and demonstrates that they stem from the inherent nonlinearity of the inversion process. We introduce a novel method to identify and mitigate these algorithmic biases, which are often mistaken for genuine physical phenomena. By applying this approach to the reconstruction of the solar vector magnetic field, we successfully eliminate the spurious effects, thereby enhancing the reliability of the resulting measurements.

This paper investigates the Boolean structures of involutions, which are defined as the Boolean algebras formed by the conjugacy classes of involutions within a finite group $G$. The study establishes that these structures are isomorphic to the Boolean algebras of conjugacy classes of involutions in the symmetric group $S_n$ if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $S_n$ itself. Furthermore, the authors provide a complete classification of all finite groups $G$ for which the Boolean structure of involutions is isomorphic to the Boolean structure of conjugacy classes of involutions in $S_n$.

This study investigates timelike Bertrand curves within semi-Riemannian spaces, focusing on the conditions under which a timelike curve qualifies as a Bertrand curve. The analysis reveals that a timelike curve is a Bertrand curve if and only if its curvature and torsion satisfy a specific linear relationship. Furthermore, the paper provides a complete classification of these curves, demonstrating that they are either helices or circular helices.

This study investigates how modifying the loss function affects classification performance in deep learning models. We examine the impact of replacing the standard cross-entropy loss with the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, which is mathematically equivalent to cross-entropy when the true class distribution is known. Our findings indicate that while this substitution does not significantly alter the final classification accuracy, it does change the internal dynamics of the model. Specifically, the models trained with KL divergence exhibit distinct behaviors regarding the evolution of their internal representations and the resulting decision boundaries compared to those trained with cross-entropy.

This paper introduces ATOMIC, a novel framework designed to enhance the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) through the use of a curated knowledge base. ATOMIC functions as an atlas of machine common knowledge, specifically focusing on if-then inference. The system is built upon a dataset comprising 10,000 instances of if-then reasoning tasks, which were generated by applying a rigorous, multi-stage process to extract and refine knowledge from existing literature. The authors demonstrate that integrating ATOMIC into an LLM significantly improves performance on reasoning benchmarks, achieving a 10.5% increase in accuracy on the ProofWriter dataset and a 12.5% improvement on the RuleTaker dataset. Furthermore, the study reveals that the framework's effectiveness is largely driven by its capacity to facilitate the application of abstract reasoning rules, thereby enabling models to generalize across diverse scenarios.

This study introduces a novel approach to video prediction that leverages a dual representation of the input data. The proposed method employs a two-stage architecture: initially, a pre-trained video encoder generates a latent representation, which is then processed by a dedicated prediction module to forecast the subsequent frame. This framework is designed to be versatile, accommodating both supervised and unsupervised learning paradigms. Furthermore, the model demonstrates robust performance across various scenarios, including those with limited training data and those involving significant domain shifts.

The metric dimension of a graph $G$ is defined as the smallest cardinality of a resolving set for $G$. A resolving set is a subset of vertices $W$ such that every vertex in $G$ is uniquely identified by its vector of distances to the elements of $W$. This paper introduces the concept of the shortened metric dimension, which is the minimum size of a resolving set $W$ where the subgraph induced by $W$ is a tree. We establish that the shortened metric dimension of a graph $G$ is at most the metric dimension of $G$ plus one. Furthermore, we provide a polynomial-time algorithm to compute the shortened metric dimension for any given graph.

This study introduces a novel deep learning framework designed to classify heart sounds, specifically targeting the detection of additive interference and convoluted deformations. The proposed architecture integrates a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a recurrent neural network (RNN) to effectively manage the challenges posed by these complex signal distortions. To validate the efficacy of this approach, the model was evaluated using a dataset comprising 1,000 heart sound recordings, each containing 10 seconds of audio. The results demonstrate that the CNN-RNN combination achieves a classification accuracy of 98.5%, surpassing the performance of other existing methods.

This study introduces a novel approach to the ASEP velocity procedure, which is a specific type of stochastic process defined on a one-dimensional lattice. The method is designed to facilitate the analysis of the system's behavior under various boundary conditions. By employing this technique, we successfully derive the exact stationary distribution for the ASEP model when subject to open boundary conditions. Furthermore, the procedure is utilized to demonstrate the existence of a phase transition within the system.

The rapid development of mathematical models for infectious diseases has been driven by the urgent need to understand and control the current SARS-CoV-2 epidemic. This paper offers a critical review of the primary modeling frameworks used to analyze the epidemic's dynamics, specifically examining the strengths and limitations of compartmental approaches, agent-based simulations, and network models. Furthermore, it explores the practical application of these frameworks in addressing key challenges, including the evaluation of non-pharmaceutical interventions, the assessment of vaccine efficacy, and the investigation of the virus's evolutionary trajectory.

The correlation between stellar mass and star formation rate (M*-SFR) exhibits a characteristic turnover at high stellar masses, a phenomenon widely attributed to the quenching of star formation in massive galaxies. While the specific mechanisms driving this decline remain debated, the role of bulges is frequently invoked as a potential cause. This study investigates the influence of bulges on the M*-SFR relation by analyzing a sample of 1,000 galaxies drawn from the SPARC database. Our findings reveal that the M*-SFR relation for bulge-dominated galaxies displays a steeper decline compared to that of disk-dominated galaxies. Furthermore, we observe that the M*-SFR relation for bulge-dominated systems is significantly steeper than the relation for disk-dominated galaxies when the latter is corrected for bulge mass. These results suggest that the presence of bulges plays a crucial role in shaping the M*-SFR relation, likely by facilitating the rapid removal of gas from the galaxy.

This study introduces a novel multi-task learning framework designed to enhance cross-language sentiment analysis. The proposed approach leverages a shared representation layer to facilitate the transfer of sentiment knowledge from English to Chinese. By incorporating auxiliary tasks—specifically sentiment classification and sentiment intensity prediction—the model effectively captures nuanced sentiment information. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that this method outperforms existing cross-language sentiment analysis techniques, achieving state-of-the-art results.

The formation of the Solar System's architecture remains a significant challenge for current theories of planet formation. While the inner Solar System is dominated by terrestrial planets, the outer regions are characterized by gas giants and ice giants. A key difficulty in explaining this structure lies in the fact that the protoplanetary disk from which the planets formed was likely too massive to be fully consumed by the planets themselves. Consequently, the remaining material must have been expelled from the system. This paper proposes a new mechanism to account for this expulsion: the interaction between the planets and the disk's outer edge, known as the "facade." The authors suggest that the planets' migration through the disk caused the facade to spin up, leading to its eventual ejection. This process would have cleared the outer disk, leaving behind the observed planetary configuration.

The rapid proliferation of deepfakes and synthetic media has intensified the spread of misinformation, creating an urgent need for automated detection systems. While existing methods have shown promise, they often struggle with generalization when encountering novel data sources or unseen generation techniques. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a novel multimodal framework designed to detect counterfeit news by learning from diverse sources and generation methods. Our approach employs a meta-learning architecture that combines neural process networks with a multimodal encoder, enabling the model to adapt to new data sources and generation techniques with minimal exposure. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches, achieving superior generalization across various unseen sources and generation techniques.

This paper introduces a novel construction for polyphase Golay complementary structures (PGCS) by combining a specific class of Golay complementary sequences (GCS) with a distinct class of Golay complementary sequences (GCS). The proposed method is demonstrated to be effective for PGCS with lengths of $2^m$ and $2^m+2^k$, where $m$ and $k$ are positive integers. Additionally, the study provides a concrete example of a PGCS with length $2^m+2^k$ and a specific construction for PGCS with length $2^m+2^k+2^k$.

This study introduces a novel method for generating cerebral lesions using a Progressive Adversarial Variational Auto-Encoder (PAVAE). The proposed model integrates a Progressive Variational Auto-Encoder (PVAE) with an adversarial framework to enhance the realism of synthetic lesions. The PVAE is designed to progressively learn the underlying data distribution, while the adversarial component ensures the generated lesions closely resemble those found in actual medical images. Experimental results demonstrate that the PAVAE outperforms existing techniques in both visual quality and quantitative metrics, making it a valuable tool for augmenting datasets and advancing research in medical image analysis.

Attribute extraction is a critical task in knowledge graph construction, yet existing methods often struggle with the challenge of diverse attribute types. To address this, we introduce a unified framework that leverages contrastive learning to extract attributes from text. Our approach begins by training a pre-trained language model to learn the semantic representations of attributes. Subsequently, we employ a contrastive learning strategy to align these representations with those of the corresponding entities. This alignment is achieved through a dual mechanism: a contrastive loss function that minimizes the distance between matching attribute-entity pairs, and a negative sampling technique that maximizes the distance between non-matching pairs. We evaluated our method on the OpenIE dataset, demonstrating that it outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques. Furthermore, we conducted an analysis of the learned representations, revealing that the proposed framework effectively captures the semantic nuances of various attribute types.

Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities across various tasks, yet their performance often degrades when handling extensive, multi-step reasoning problems. To address this, we introduce SKILL, a novel framework designed to enhance LLMs' reasoning abilities by integrating structured insights into the generation process. SKILL operates by decomposing complex reasoning tasks into smaller, manageable sub-tasks, allowing the model to generate intermediate reasoning steps that are subsequently refined through a dedicated skill module. This module employs a structured approach to analyze and improve these intermediate steps, ensuring the final output is both logically sound and coherent. We evaluated SKILL on the GSM8K and MATH datasets, where it achieved state-of-the-art results, surpassing existing methods by 1.5% and 2.5% respectively. Furthermore, our analysis indicates that SKILL significantly improves the interpretability of model outputs, offering clearer insights into the reasoning process.

We examine the thermodynamic behavior of non-linear charged AdS black holes by analyzing their shadow characteristics. Our findings reveal that the shadow radius exhibits a linear relationship with the Hawking temperature, mirroring the behavior observed in linearly charged AdS black holes. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the shadow radius increases as the non-linear parameter rises, indicating that non-linear electrodynamics enhances the black hole's thermodynamic entropy. Additionally, we observe that the shadow radius grows with increasing charge and decreases as the AdS curvature parameter increases. Finally, we establish a connection between the shadow radius and the black hole's entropy, showing that the shadow radius serves as a reliable indicator of the black hole's thermodynamic entropy.

This study examines the evolution of quantum entanglement and the onset of synchronization within a two-mode bosonic system, where the dynamics are governed by a Hamiltonian featuring a quadratic interaction between the modes and a linear coupling to an external field. The analysis employs the Wigner function and the quantum tomogram as primary tools for investigation. The findings demonstrate that the system's entanglement undergoes a transition from a non-monotonic to a monotonic behavior as the external field strength increases. Furthermore, the research reveals that synchronization emerges in the system when the external field reaches a specific threshold value.

We report the first observation of the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ decay, achieved with a statistical significance of 5.0 standard deviations using data collected by the LHCb experiment at the LHC. This result is based on an integrated luminosity of 3.0 fb$^{-1}$ recorded at a center-of-mass energy of 7 TeV. Additionally, we present evidence for the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decay, observed with a significance of 3.0 standard deviations. The measured branching fractions for these processes are determined to be $\mathcal{B}(B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S) = (1.01 \pm 0.14 \pm 0.10) \times 10^{-4}$ and $\mathcal{B}(B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S) = (1.01 \pm 0.14 \pm 0.10) \times 10^{-4}$, where the first uncertainty reflects statistical variation and the second accounts for systematic effects.

This paper addresses the challenge of reconstructing the submodule lattice for a multiplicity-free module when only partial data is available. Specifically, it examines the scenario where the lattice is known for a single composition factor, while the lattice for the entire module remains unknown. The authors demonstrate that, under these conditions, the full lattice can be successfully reconstructed. The approach involves first determining the lattice for the module's socle and then utilizing the established relationship between the submodule lattice and the lattice of subquotients to derive the complete structure.

This study investigates the existence of biharmonic hypersurfaces within Euclidean space, specifically focusing on those that satisfy a recurring operator condition. The analysis demonstrates that such hypersurfaces must be minimal. Furthermore, the paper establishes a specific relationship between the mean curvature and the recurring operator, showing that the latter is proportional to the former.

This paper introduces the concept of a $p/q$-identifiable collection, which generalizes the notion of $p$-identifiable collections. We establish that a collection is $p/q$-identifiable if and only if it is $p$-identifiable. Furthermore, we demonstrate that a collection is $p$-identifiable precisely when it is $p$-identifiable and satisfies the $p/q$-identifiable condition. Finally, we provide a necessary and sufficient condition for a collection to be $p/q$-identifiable.

We present a measurement of the differential decay rate for the $B_s^0\rightarrow D_s^{*-}\mu^{+}\nu_{\mu}$ process, utilizing data collected by the LHCb experiment at the LHC. The analysis covers the $q^2$ range from 0.0004 to 14.5 $\text{GeV}^2/c^4$, based on a dataset of 1.0 $\text{fb}^{-1}$ recorded at a center-of-mass energy of 13 $\text{TeV}$. The results are compared with predictions from the Standard Model, employing both the perturbative QCD approach and the light-cone sum rule method.

When an adhesive strip is peeled from a surface, the resulting crackling noise arises from the stick-slip dynamics of the interface. This study reveals that the acoustic signature of this process is governed by a concealed arrangement of stick-slip events, which are organized into distinct clusters. These clusters exhibit a power-law distribution in their size, indicating a scale-invariant characteristic. Furthermore, the analysis demonstrates that the stick-slip events within these clusters are not independent; instead, they display a strong positive correlation, suggesting that the occurrence of one event significantly influences the likelihood of subsequent events within the same cluster.

In 1923, Menger introduced the concept of angle spaces, which are metric spaces where the angle between two geodesics is defined via the law of cosines. He established that angle spaces are equivalent to Euclidean spaces and posed two questions: whether the angle function is uniquely determined by the metric, and if the angle function can be defined for spaces that are not angle spaces. This paper provides affirmative answers to both inquiries.

Point cloud processing is a critical task in computer vision, yet existing deep learning models often struggle with generalization when encountering point clouds that differ in size, density, or noise levels. To address this, we introduce TPC, a novel smoothing technique designed to enhance the robustness of point cloud representations. TPC operates by applying a transformation-dependent smoothing strategy that dynamically adjusts based on the specific geometric transformations applied to the data. Our approach is built upon a simple yet effective architecture: a transformer-based encoder paired with a lightweight smoothing module. We demonstrate the efficacy of TPC through extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets, showing significant improvements in classification accuracy and robustness against various geometric transformations.

This paper establishes a clear Serre weight conjecture for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over a totally real field $F$ by utilizing Kummer theory. The authors demonstrate that the conjecture holds true for all $p$-adic Galois representations that are crystalline at $p$ and unramified outside $p$.

This study introduces a novel method for reconstructing the harmonic contour of a self-sensing composite, which is composed of a conductive matrix and a piezoelectric inclusion. The approach combines electrical impedance tomography (EIT) with evolutionary algorithms to achieve this reconstruction. The proposed technique is validated through both numerical simulations and experimental testing. Results indicate that the method successfully recovers the harmonic contour of the self-sensing composite with high accuracy, demonstrating its potential for non-destructive evaluation of piezoelectric materials.

This study introduces a geometric approach to the tensor representation of a Euclidean space, offering a fresh perspective on the tensor product of two vectors. By employing this method, we derive the explicit formula for the tensor product of two vectors and demonstrate how it relates to the standard tensor product. Furthermore, we establish the connection between the tensor product and the exterior product, and we provide a geometric interpretation of the tensor product of two vectors.

This paper establishes a geometric characterization of the subgroups within right-angled Artin groups (RAAGs) that are isomorphic to RAAGs. The authors demonstrate that a subgroup of a RAAG is itself a RAAG if and only if it is a free factor of the parent group. Furthermore, the study provides a geometric description of the specific subgroups that are free factors.

This paper addresses the challenge of learning in distributed linear bandits where the objective is to identify the optimal action within a shared linear model, yet the available actions differ across agents. We introduce a novel algorithm that achieves a regret bound of $O(d\sqrt{T})$ for a single agent, where $d$ represents the dimensionality of the linear model and $T$ denotes the time horizon. Notably, this result is attained without requiring agents to share their local action sets or the specific linear models they observe.

The vertical shear instability (VSI) is a proposed mechanism for rapid planetesimal formation in the outer regions of protoplanetary disks, where the gas rotates at a sub-Keplerian speed. This paper investigates how dust development influences the VSI by examining the vertical structure of the disk and the resulting vertical velocity shear. We find that dust settling significantly reduces the vertical velocity shear, thereby weakening the VSI. However, the instability persists even when dust settles to the midplane, provided the dust-to-gas ratio remains high. Additionally, we demonstrate that the VSI can trigger dust clumping, which further enhances the instability. These findings suggest that the VSI remains a viable pathway for planetesimal formation in the outer disk regions.

This study establishes a Liouville theorem for Ricci diminutives that maintain a constant scalar curvature, demonstrating that any complete, non-compact Ricci diminutive with constant scalar curvature and non-negative sectional curvature must be flat. Furthermore, the paper explores the geometric characteristics of Ricci diminutives with constant scalar curvature and non-negative sectional curvature, proving that such spaces are either flat or possess a specific geometric structure.

This study introduces a novel architecture for dynamic image classification, termed Dynamic Entrances with Global Mean Pooling (DE-GMP). The proposed method integrates a dynamic entrance module with a global mean pooling layer to enhance the efficiency of dynamic image classification. Experimental results demonstrate that DE-GMP achieves superior performance compared to existing dynamic classification approaches, particularly when applied to large-scale datasets.

Federated learning (FL) is a machine learning technique designed to train models across distributed devices without sharing raw data, thereby addressing privacy concerns. However, existing FL methods often struggle when dealing with data drawn from diverse distributions, leading to suboptimal performance. To overcome this, we introduce Stroll for Education (Stroll), a novel algorithm that integrates a random walk strategy into the FL training process. Stroll effectively mitigates the challenges posed by non-IID data, delivering superior performance compared to current state-of-the-art approaches. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical analysis demonstrating that Stroll achieves convergence rates comparable to those of centralized learning.

This study introduces a novel consistency regularization method designed to enhance the performance of deep learning models in semi-supervised medical image segmentation. The proposed approach is built upon a straightforward yet effective framework that leverages a single teacher network to generate pseudo-labels for unlabeled data. By applying a simple yet effective consistency regularization technique, the model achieves significant improvements in segmentation accuracy. The method is evaluated on two distinct medical image datasets, demonstrating its efficacy and robustness in real-world healthcare applications.

The nonlocality of quantum mechanics is typically demonstrated through entangled states involving multiple particles, such as the EPR paradox and Bell's theorem. However, the nonlocality of single-particle entanglement remains a subject of debate. This paper demonstrates that single-particle entanglement can produce genuine nonlocal effects, specifically the nonlocal guidance of a single particle. This guidance effect is shown to be a nonlocal phenomenon that cannot be explained by local hidden variable theories.

The rapid growth of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) has created a demand for secure, efficient, and reliable communication, yet the distributed nature of IoV introduces significant challenges regarding data privacy, security, and trust. To address these issues, blockchain technology offers a promising solution by providing a decentralized, immutable ledger that ensures data integrity and transparency. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of blockchain-enabled federated education frameworks designed for IoV environments. The authors examine the core principles of these frameworks, analyze their primary applications, and evaluate existing solutions based on key performance metrics such as security, efficiency, and scalability. Furthermore, the study identifies current limitations and proposes future research directions to advance the development of robust, secure, and efficient IoV systems.

This study introduces a novel algorithm and hardware co-development strategy for energy-efficient Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks designed for video identification tasks. The proposed method leverages hierarchical Tucker tensor decomposition to optimize LSTM architectures, significantly reducing computational complexity and memory requirements. By integrating this algorithm with a custom-designed hardware accelerator, the system achieves substantial efficiency gains. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach reduces energy consumption by 40% compared to existing methods while maintaining high identification accuracy.

This study investigates the prime focus of the iterates of the composition of two polynomials, denoted as $f \circ g$. The authors establish that if $f \circ g$ possesses a prime focus, then $f$ must also have a prime focus. Furthermore, the paper provides a complete classification of the prime focus for the iterates of $f \circ g$ under the condition that $f$ is a prime focus.

This study examines the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation featuring a power-type nonlinearity within a domain defined as the exterior of a convex barrier. The analysis demonstrates that, for sufficiently large initial data, the solution exhibits finite-time blow-up. Furthermore, the paper establishes a lower bound for the blow-up rate and proves that the solution's gradient becomes unbounded at the singularity.

This study establishes a positive-characteristic semi-parametric local-uniform version of the theorem by Kollár and Mori regarding the existence of a uniform, positive-characteristic semi-parametric local-uniform abbreviation for varieties defined over finitely produced $\mathbb{Q}$-algebras.

Bayes factors serve as a robust tool for comparing models, yet their practical application is often hindered by the high computational costs associated with the required integrals. This paper introduces a suite of strategies designed to streamline the calculation of Bayes factors, specifically targeting scenarios where the underlying models are complex and lack closed-form solutions. The proposed workflow integrates several key components: a novel, efficient algorithm for estimating marginal likelihoods; a method for approximating the posterior distribution of the Bayes factor itself; and a technique for generating synthetic data to facilitate the estimation of prior predictive distributions. To demonstrate the efficacy of these strategies, the authors apply them to a range of models, including those with intricate structures and those involving latent variables.

Discourse markers, such as "however" and "therefore," are essential for conveying the logical relationships between sentences, yet their interpretation often depends heavily on context. This paper introduces DiscSense, a novel framework designed to automatically analyze the semantic roles of discourse markers within specific contexts. The system operates through a two-stage process: first, it identifies the semantic function of a marker using a pre-trained language model, and second, it refines this function by incorporating contextual information via a fine-tuned BERT model. Evaluated on the Discourse Sense Test (DST) dataset, DiscSense demonstrates superior performance compared to existing methods, achieving an F1 score of 78.4% and an accuracy of 76.1%. These results highlight the framework's effectiveness in capturing nuanced semantic meanings and its potential for advancing discourse analysis in natural language processing.

This study introduces a one-parameter family of Jordanian twists, denoted as $F_{\lambda}$, which are constructed from the Jordanian twist $F$ and the universal $R$-matrix of the quantum group $U_{q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2})$. We demonstrate that $F_{\lambda}$ satisfies the 2-cocycle condition and constitutes a twist of $F$ for all $\lambda$ in the interval $[0,1]$. Furthermore, we establish that $F_{\lambda}$ is a twist of $F$ for any $\lambda \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \{0\}$. Finally, we examine the relationship between $F_{\lambda}$ and the Drinfeld twist $F_{\text{Dr}}$ associated with the Drinfeld twist $F_{\text{Dr}}$.

This paper introduces a symbolic algorithm designed to solve extended regular expression inequalities, which encompass the standard Kleene star, union, concatenation, and complement operations. The proposed method is both sound and complete, relying on a novel symbolic representation of regular languages and a symbolic decision procedure for the emptiness problem. Furthermore, the algorithm is capable of handling the extended Kleene star, a feature absent in the original regular expression framework. The approach is implemented within the tool called SREX, which has been validated against existing solutions and demonstrates superior performance.

Lobster-eye optics, which utilize the total external reflection of X-rays from the inner surfaces of V-shaped microstructures, are well-suited for wide-field imaging and spectroscopy. This study introduces a novel multiplexing technique that combines several lobster-eye modules into a single system to achieve extensive field-of-view coverage. The proposed design features a 1-meter diameter primary mirror composed of 16 lobster-eye modules, each with a 6.25-meter diameter, arranged in a hexagonal configuration. This arrangement enables a total field-of-view of 1.5 degrees. The paper details the design, fabrication, and testing of a prototype module, which successfully demonstrated a 0.5-degree field-of-view and a 100% effective area at 1.5 keV. Furthermore, the authors present a simulation of the full 1-meter system, predicting a 0.5-degree field-of-view and a 100% effective area at 1.5 keV. This multiplexing approach offers a promising solution for constructing large-area X-ray telescopes with wide-field capabilities.

This study investigates the function of the cosmic speed field (CSF) in the mass distribution of dark matter halos. We find that the CSF is a crucial factor in determining the mass distribution of dark matter halos, with its influence becoming more pronounced as the mass of the dark matter halo increases. Additionally, we observe that the CSF exhibits a strong correlation with the mass of dark matter halos, and this correlation intensifies with increasing halo mass. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the CSF can be used to predict the mass of dark matter halos with high accuracy. These results suggest that the CSF is a significant factor in the mass distribution of dark matter halos and may provide valuable insights into the formation and evolution of dark matter halos.

This study demonstrates the capability of an atomic interferometer to detect minute magnetic field variations within a superconducting Meissner shield. By measuring the phase shift induced by a magnetic field change of 10 nT, the experiment achieved a sensitivity of 1.5 nT/√Hz at a 1-second integration time. This level of detection is made possible by the high magnetic field sensitivity inherent to the atomic interferometer, combined with the exceptional magnetic shielding provided by the superconducting material.

This study presents a relativistic initial principles investigation into the electronic and magnetic characteristics of Yu--Shiba--Rusinov (YSR) states, focusing on Mn adatoms and Mn dimers situated on a Nb(110) surface. The analysis reveals that the YSR states exhibit a pronounced dependence on the magnetic orientation of the Mn adatom or dimer relative to the Nb(110) surface. Furthermore, the findings demonstrate that the magnetic anisotropy energy of the Mn adatom and dimer is significantly influenced by the presence of these YSR states.

Skin cancer is a prevalent and potentially fatal condition, with early detection being critical for effective treatment. This study introduces a novel deep learning framework designed to identify skin cancer from dermoscopic images, specifically addressing the challenge of detecting outlier samples caused by data collection errors. The proposed method employs a two-stage architecture: first, a deep neural network classifies images as either cancerous or non-cancerous; second, a dedicated outlier detection module identifies samples that deviate from the standard classification patterns. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach achieves a 99.7% accuracy rate in identifying skin cancer and successfully detects 99.5% of outlier samples.

This study introduces a novel, computationally efficient method for estimating vector boson polarization in high-energy muon interactions. The approach relies on a simplified, approximate formula for the differential cross-section, which is derived from the full expression by retaining only the leading-order terms in the scattering angle. This approximation is valid for the specific kinematic regime where the scattering angle is small and the center-of-mass energy is high. The resulting formula is significantly more efficient to compute than the exact version, making it particularly suitable for large-scale Monte Carlo simulations. Furthermore, the paper demonstrates that this simplified model accurately reproduces the polarization of the vector boson across the entire scattering angle range.

This paper offers a fresh perspective on the Rosser sentence, a pivotal result in mathematical logic that extends Tarski's theorem on the undefinability of truth. The authors demonstrate that the Rosser sentence can be derived from a specific, weaker assumption regarding the existence of a truth predicate. This assumption is notably less demanding than the full Tarski truth definition, requiring only that the predicate be defined for all sentences that are not themselves defined by the predicate. The authors also explore the relationship between the Rosser sentence and the Liar paradox, showing that the Rosser sentence can be constructed from the Liar sentence by adding a single, straightforward condition.

This study examines the existence of invariant surfaces within fractional order dynamical systems, specifically those defined by the Caputo derivative. We demonstrate that, unlike in integer order systems, invariant surfaces do not exist for fractional order systems when the order is strictly less than one. This result is established through a proof by contradiction, which relies on the uniqueness of solutions for fractional differential equations.

This study addresses the inverse problem of reconstructing the acoustic pressure field within a fluid domain, given the structural displacement of a submerged elastic plate. The proposed methodology employs a reduced-order model (ROM) to represent the fluid dynamics, which is then integrated into a gradient-based optimization framework. This approach facilitates the reconstruction of the acoustic field using only a limited number of pressure measurements. The efficacy of the method is demonstrated through a numerical example involving a submerged plate, where the reconstruction is achieved using just two pressure sensors.

This study examines the simplest scoto-seesaw model, which incorporates a single right-handed neutrino and a single scalar singlet to generate neutrino masses. We demonstrate that this framework offers a viable solution to the dark matter problem, with the scalar singlet serving as the dark matter candidate. Our analysis reveals that the model can simultaneously account for dark matter relic abundance, neutrino oscillation data, and the observed Higgs boson mass. Furthermore, we show that the vacuum stability of the Higgs potential is maintained across the entire parameter space.
